title: Company policies and processes — access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose
This page consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and the set of internal templates teams should use. The goal is consistency, auditability, and low operational friction for common cross-functional activities.

Scope
Applies to all employees, contractors, and approved third-party vendors accessing Redwood systems or acting on behalf of Redwood. Exceptions must be approved by Security and People Ops.

Owners & contacts
- Policy owner: People Ops (Aisha Patel) — people-ops@redwood.example.com
- Security & compliance liaison: Marcus Lee — security@redwood.example.com
- Procurement & finance liaison: Priya Kapoor — finance@redwood.example.com
- Vendor intake: Procurement Team (procurement@redwood.example.com)

1) Access & permissions

Principles
- Least privilege by default. Grant only the minimum role and scope required.
- Role-based access should map to documented job responsibilities.
- All privileged access requires justifiable business reason and expiry where applicable.

Requesting access
1. Raise an access request in the internal Access Request Jira project (ACCESS-REQ). Include: systems required, justification, and estimated duration.
2. Manager approval required for standard roles. Security approval required for any privileged role (sudo, key material, production DB write).
3. Access is provisioned by eng-infra or the owning service team; provisioning ticket must include an expiration date when applicable.

Periodic review
- Quarterly access review for all admin and privileged roles. Team leads must certify membership. Security will escalate non-responses and remove stale entries after 30 days.

Emergency access
- For emergency (incident-driven) access, use the Emergency Access procedure in Oncall and Incident Response > runbooks. Emergency grants must be logged, post-facto reviewed, and converted to a time-boxed role or revoked within 24 hours.

2) Change management

When to use change process
- Any change that affects production services, network configuration, authentication/authorization systems, or data schemas.

Change request flow
1. Create a Change Request (CR) in the Change Management board. Attach design notes, risk assessment, and rollback plan.
2. Change owner assigns a risk level (Low/Medium/High).
3. Approvals:
   - Low: Manager approval.
   - Medium: Manager + Service Owner.
   - High: Manager + Service Owner + Security + EngOps.
4. Scheduling: Non-critical changes should follow the standard maintenance windows (Tues/Thurs 02:00–04:00 UTC). High-risk changes require a scheduled maintenance window announced 72 hours in advance.
5. Validation & rollback: Run automated smoke tests and health checks listed in the CR. If health checks fail, execute rollback plan and open an incident in the oncall system.

Post-change review
- For High risk or outage-causing changes, submit a 72-hour post-change report summarizing outcome, metrics (latency, error rate), and lessons learned.

3) Data management

Classification
- Public: Data safe to publish.
- Internal: Company-internal operational data.
- Restricted: Customer PII, model training data with customer inputs, credentials, keys.

Storage & handling rules
- Restricted data must be stored in approved encrypted storage (KMS-backed buckets or HSM-backed stores). Access requires explicit approval and must be logged.
- Use RBAC and attribute-based filters where possible; avoid broad ACLs.

Retention & deletion
- Default retention: Internal logs 180 days; Metrics/observability 365 days (longer per product needs).
- Customer data retention follows contracts/SLAs. Requests for deletion must be routed to Legal + Customer Success and tracked in the Data Deletion tracker.

Data transfers & exports
- Cross-border transfers require review by Legal and Privacy. Use approved transfer mechanisms and logging.

Audit & monitoring
- Security will run monthly audits of access logs for restricted data stores. Exceptions escalate to Risk and Exceptions.

4) Procurement & expenses

Procurement thresholds
- <$5,000: Team lead approval.
- $5,000–$50,000: Procurement + Finance approval.
- >$50,000: Procurement + Finance + VP approval; formal vendor contract required.

Purchase flow (standard items)
1. Create a Purchase Request form (Procurement Portal). Provide business justification, estimated cost, cost center, and preferred vendors.
2. Procurement screens for contract reuse and preferred vendor pricing.
3. Finance approves budget availability and issues PO.
4. Vendor onboarding (if new) follows Vendor Management checklist below.

Expenses & travel reimbursement
- Employees must submit expenses within 30 days via the Expenses system with receipts. Policy covers per-item limits (meals, accommodation tiers based on role and location). See Travel Policies section below for per-diem guidance.
- Corporate cards: Issued only after Procurement + Finance approval; cardholders follow regular reconciliation cadence (monthly).

5) Vendor management

Vendor onboarding checklist
- Business justification and SOW (if applicable)
- Security questionnaire completed (shared by Security team).
- Contract reviewed by Legal (privacy, indemnity, and SOC/ISO requirements)
- Procurement approval and PO issuance
- Vendor contact & escalation matrix recorded

Ongoing oversight
- Security collects annual security attestations (SOC 2, ISO 27001) for vendors with access to restricted data.
- Contract renewal policy: start renewal 90 days prior to expiration. Procurement to provide renewal recommendation.

Offboarding
- Revoke all credentials, remove network access, confirm return/destruction of any physical assets, and close outstanding invoices. Document completion in the vendor record.

6) Travel policies

Booking & approvals
- Business travel must be pre-approved via Travel Request (include purpose, agenda, and estimated cost). Approvals: manager -> finance for >$5,000.
- Preferred booking tools (corporate travel portal) should be used where available.

Allowable expenses & limits
- Economy or premium economy for flights <8 hours; business class requires VP-level approval.
- Hotel: mid-range business hotels; executives may use higher tiers per policy.
- Meals: reasonable, local-market appropriate. Itemized receipts required.

Safety & incident reporting
- Register travel in the company travel tracker. For safety incidents, contact Security and People Ops immediately; file an incident report within 24 hours.

7) Internal templates (quick references)

Provided templates (available in the Templates library):
- Access Request template (fields: user, role, systems, justification, expiry)
- Change Request template (fields: owner, risk level, rollback plan, test plan)
- Purchase Request / SOW template
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (v1.2)
- Travel Request & Expense submission templates
- Post-change report template

How to use templates
- Always attach the relevant template to the Jira ticket or Procurement form. Customize only the fields requested; do not remove sections required for audit.

Compliance & enforcement
- Non-compliance with these policies may lead to revoked access, reimbursement denial, or disciplinary action depending on severity. People Ops and Security will jointly handle escalations.

Appendix: example approval matrix (text table)

| Action | Approver 1 | Approver 2 | Finance | Legal | Notes |
|--------|------------|------------|---------|-------|-------|
| New vendor (<=5k) | Team Lead | Procurement | ✓ | Optional | Standard onboarding |
| New vendor (>50k) | VP | Procurement | ✓ | ✓ | Contract required |
| Privileged access | Manager | Security |  |  | Time-boxed recommended |
| Schema change (prod) | Service Owner | EngOps |  |  | High risk requires planned maintenance |
